key_insight: Human and LLM collaboration can accelerate materials synthesis by generating experimentally testable recipes, but success depends strongly on whether the target material is already well understood.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that closed-loop human–AI workflows can improve materials discovery pipelines by rapidly iterating between recipe generation and lab validation for complex solid-state synthesis.
method: Generated synthesis recipes for known and unknown Ruddlesden-Popper materials using both humans and an LLM
Executed the proposed recipes in the lab and scored success experimentally
Fed results back into a second round of human and LLM recipe generation in a closed-loop comparison
evidence_signal: Experimental success rates were reported for humans vs LLMs across known and unknown materials in two rounds, with higher success for known materials than unknown ones and a discovered new material, Ba3PtO5.
watch_item: Performance drops sharply on unknown targets, so recipe generation may still require strong human oversight and domain constraints for novel structure types.
paper_title: Human and LLM Collaboration for Accelerated Materials Synthesis and Discovery
